This paper conducts a comparative multimodal discourse analysis of Barbie (2023) by examining technological roles in the feminist Barbieland and patriarchal Kenland to uncover the relationship between technology and gender ideologies. Using Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) and Feminist CDA, the study employs Iedema's (2001) film genre analysis for layering technological representations across scenes for data collection and Van Leeuwen's (2008) Toy Social Actor Network assess how technologies signify gendered power structures.Three key findings emerge. First, Barbieland's technologies—used for careers, daily routines, and humanitarian purposes — promote inclusivity, feminist empowerment and social equality. In contrast, patriarchal Kenland's technologies serve masculine exclusivity, domination, and competition. Second, while Barbies employ technology carefully and collaboratively for communal benefit, Kens weaponize it violently to assert sovereignty — feminist collectivity versus patriarchal aggression. Third, aesthetic differences reinforce ideological divides. Barbieland's pink, plastic, and smooth-textured technologies signify fantasy and benevolence for matriarchal ideals, whereas Kenland's darker, concrete, and functional designs embody realism, rejecting Barbie's utopianism. Additionally, naming practices reveal deeper ideological contrasts. Barbies' generically labeled "dream houses" and vehicles signify inclusivity, while Kens' specifically named "Mojo Dojo Casa House" and race cars enforce exclusion. The renaming of vehicles to "K.B" signals feminist reconfiguration toward coexistence rather than oppression.The study concludes that technology in Barbie operates as a semiotic tool to both reinforce and challenge gendered hierarchies.

In November 1818, John Keats wrote a short note to Mrs. Davenport, expressing concern for his brother and thanking her for her kindness. This simple letter reveals interesting details about Keats's neighbours in Hampstead. The Davenports ran a silversmith business and lived on Church Row, where another notable feminist writer, Anna Laeticia Barbauld, also lived.Keats's family background is linked to a radical church, yet only two scholars have devoted book length studies to London's religious milieu during his time alive. To bridge this gap in knowledge, my paper will explore whether the nonconformist religious beliefs from Keats's childhood influenced his poetry – an understanding, I argue – that comes with familiarising ourselves with his Hampstead neighbours.

The transition from childhood to young adulthood is a complex period of adaptation and change. With adequate external motivation, such as encouragement and recognition from significant adults, youth can develop a strong sense of self and maintain positive mental health. This presentation will share findings from a community-based participatory research project conducted in Alberta, Canada, and Hong Kong. The three-year project engaged youth aged 12 to 17 in exploring issues related to mental health and well-being. This Children and Youth Mental Health (CYMH) project comprised four key components: photo storytelling groups, web-app co-creation groups, community forums, and an international symposium. A strong emphasis was placed on youth training and mentorship throughout the project. Over 200 youth from both locations actively participated in various stages of the project. This presentation will highlight the collaborative governance framework developed and the transformative experiences of youth involved.

Dr. Kwok is currently the Associate Director of the School of Public Policy at the University of Calgary. He previously served as the Associate Dean (Undergraduate Programs) and Associate Dean (Southern Alberta Region) in the Faculty of Social Work. In this role he was responsible for the strategic direction and academic quality of all the social work undergraduate programs, which includes campuses in Calgary, Edmonton, Lethbridge; programs at Red Deer, Medicine Hat, and Grande Prairie; and the online program. Before he joined the University of Calgary in 2016, he was a Professor at King's University College at Western University and was the Academic Director of the Southwestern Regional Hub of Ontario, Youth Research and Evaluation Exchange (YouthREX) which is funded by Ontario's Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services and housed in King's University College at Western University. He holds a Diploma of Social Work from City University of Hong Kong, a Bachelor of Social Work from Hong Kong Polytechnic University, a Master of Social Work from University of British Columbia, a Doctor of Philosophy in Social Work from University of Calgary, and a Master of Public Administration from Western University. His commitment to his field and support of his peers is demonstrated by his election as the President of Alberta College of Social Workers (ACSW), which is the regulatory body of the social work profession under the Health Professions Act in the province of Alberta. In his career, he has received numerous research and teaching awards, invited to present at national and international conferences as a keynote and panelist member, and has testified at the Canadian Standing Senate Committee on Human Rights on the topic of visible minorities and the criminal justice system.

This presentation defines shared parenting as an arrangement in which a child spends at least 40% of their time with each parent. Domestic violence, or intimate partner violence, is defined by the United Nations as "a pattern of behavior in any relationship that is used to gain or maintain power and control over an intimate partner." Young children are defined as those under the age of four. Using an intersectoral perspective, this presentation examines the complex experiences of mothers before and after shared parenting arrangements are established. It focuses on women survivors of domestic violence who are raising at least one young child and share parenting responsibilities with their ex-husband or ex-partner. In addition to addressing the challenges faced, the presentation highlights the resilience and coping strategies demonstrated by these women. Implications for social work practice will be discussed, with particular emphasis on promoting safety, empowerment, and child well-being.

Professor Dora Tam is a well-recognized scholar in the Faculty of Social Work at the University of Calgary, specializing in research and practice related to women and child survivors of domestic violence, as well as child and youth mental health. She has secured numerous national and international research grants and is acknowledged for her expertise in mixed-methods and participatory action research methodologies. Professor Tam served as the Principal Investigator for an international research project entitled Collaborative Health Initiatives to Prevent and Intervene in Violence against Women in China. In 2018, she co-founded the Social Work Innovation Hub, an initiative designed to promote interdisciplinary and transnational partnerships between Canada, China, and other international partners. Between 2020 and 2023, she led a three-year international research initiative examining evidence-based practices to improve mental health outcomes among children and youth in Canada and China. Professor Tam has published extensively in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals, including serving as lead author on Racial Minority Women and the Criminal Justice Response to Domestic Violence in Canada and Social Work Interventions on Intimate Partner Violence against Women in China. Her scholarship continues to shape social work practice in the areas of child and family welfare, mental health, and violence prevention.Date : 20thJun 2025 (Friday)Time:  3:30pm-5:30pmVenue:Room  A103

Stickers are widely used in digital communication to enhance emotional and visual expressions. The conventional process of creating new sticker pack images involves time-consuming manual drawing, including meticulous color coordination and shading techniques for visual harmony. Learning the visual styles of distinct sticker packs would be critical to the overall process; however, existing solutions usually learn this style information within a limited number of style "domains", or per image. In this work, we propose a contrastive learning framework that allows the style editing of an arbitrary sticker based on one or a number of style references with a continuous manifold to encapsulate all styles across sticker packs. The key to our approach is the encoding of styles into a unified latent space so that each sticker pack correlates with a unique style latent encoding. The contrastive loss ensures identical style latents within the same sticker pack, while distinct styles diverge. Through exposure to diverse sticker sets during training, our model crafts a consolidated continuous latent style space with strong expressive power, fostering seamless style transfer, interpolation, and mixing across sticker sets.

Guidelines play an important role in calligraphy study since they allow beginners to get an idea of how the calligraphic strokes are formed and how to write a calligraphic stroke. However, manually generating guidelines for calligraphic characters is tedious, so only limited calligraphic books with guidelines provided are available. To automatically generate the guidelines, one needs to first decompose the strokes from the character and then automatically generate guideline for each stroke. However, this is very challenging since the existing guideline generation methods only mimic the shapes of the guidelines, but generally cannot produce precise guidelines that can be practically used for amateurs to trace the calligraphic strokes. In this paper, we first adopt a state-of-the-art stroke segmentation method based on the information of stroke categories. Then we propose a novel guideline generation method by fitting ellipse-shaped brushes to each stroke based on contour tangents. Extensive visual and quantitative experiments have been conducted to validate the effectiveness of our method. Results and statistics show that our method outperforms existing methods both visually and quantitatively.

This paper outlines a 2020-2021 policy study in Hong Kong targeting at-risk informal caregivers of frail elders, emphasizing prompt identification and support. Findings revealed that sudden caregiving distress often arose from disruptions like COVID-19, service changes, or care recipient health shifts. Current services were insufficiently responsive, prioritizing caregiving tasks over caregiver well-being. Low respite service uptake despite high demand underscored the need for improved caregiver-focused services. Recommendations included a 24-hour caregiver hotline and diverse respite care options. As a result, a hotline has been funded by the government. Yet, further exploration is warranted for user-friendly respite care solutions.

Tragic incidents related to informal caregiving have often been linked to families from lower socio-economic backgrounds who lack support resources. However, a 2024 case involving a wealthy older woman attempting murder-suicide with her chronically ill husband challenges this notion. This presentation investigates service utilisation patterns among carers in Hong Kong and explores a new case management model to meet evolving needs. Fieldwork from 2022-2024 included focus groups and interviews with over 70 informal carers. A common theme emerged: carers' fears of becoming ill themselves, leading to stress and anxiety. This paper proposes a framework to help carers plan for future caregiving responsibilities systematically.

This randomized controlled equivalence trial compared the ambulation abilities of patients after hip fracture. The study group received five physiotherapy visits at home and the control group was rehabilitated in an institution for 30 days. The results indicated that the domiciliary group achieved comparable or superior ambulation outcomes with lower direct costs, suggesting that home-based rehabilitation is a viable alternative. This approach not only accelerated hospital discharge but also promoted functional recovery, enhancing the quality of life for older patients post-fracture. Findings supported the continuation of domiciliary physiotherapy in similar patient populations.

Globally, problematic levels of loneliness are experienced by a substantial proportion of the world's population, particularly older people. In older people, loneliness increases the risk of developing physical diseases, dementia-related disorders and mental health problems, including depression. Despite the high prevalence of loneliness in older people in Hong Kong, little is known about the relationship between loneliness, psychological resilience, and depression in this population. In this seminar, the findings of a cross-sectional study which examined levels of loneliness, psychological resilience and depression in 210 community-dwelling older people in Hong Kong will be presented. These findings may facilitate the development of interventions, including resilience-building strategies, to target aspects of loneliness to enhance well-being of older adults in Hong Kong.

Stroke is a leading cause of disability in Hong Kong, and the high population density and active lifestyles of residents place them at significant risk. While conventional stroke rehabilitation approaches have been utilized, they often fail to fully address the unique needs and circumstances of individual patients. In contrast, personalized rehabilitation strategies hold great promise for enhancing patient outcomes, improving satisfaction, and reducing treatment costs by tailoring interventions to the specific requirements of each stroke survivor.

This comprehensive review article provides an in-depth examination of the current state of personalized stroke rehabilitation in Hong Kong.It analyzes key aspects such as the development of individualized therapy plans, the utilization of multidisciplinary care teams, the integration of innovative technologies, and the active engagement of patients and their caregivers. By drawing upon the latest research evidence and insights from experienced professionals, the article summarizes best practices, identifies areas for further advancement, and proposes strategies for implementing more comprehensive, patient-centered models of stroke rehabilitation. The findings presented in this review have significant implications for improving stroke care not only in Hong Kong, but also in other densely populated urban centers facing similar challenges.

This presentation discusses the incorporation of informal caregiving into healthcare professional curricula, focusing on physiotherapy. Informal caregivers, often family and friends, play a crucial role in rehabilitation, yet are frequently overlooked. We'll highlight the importance of recognizing caregivers' needs and challenges, and their impact on patient outcomes.

The presentation outlines strategies to enhance physiotherapy education, including integrating case studies, simulation-based learning and interprofessional education workshops to foster collaboration between physiotherapists and informal caregivers. By equipping future physiotherapists with the skills to engage effectively with caregivers, we aim to promote a holistic approach to patient care.Date : 17thFebrary 2025 (Monday)Time:  10:00am-12:00pmVenue: CBCC Rm 526Poster

In the context of the first anniversary of the elevation of our Institution as a University, and after being granted the title of "University of Applied Sciences", the considerations on the implications and ethical challenges of research work in our Catholic inspired institution of higher education is very important.I will share my reflections on the role of research in academy; its relationship with the core values of Saint Francis University, especially truth, and some basic elements that Catholic education proposes in the development of research projects.

Tips for Submitting Research Ethics ApplicationsThe Research and Ethics Committee addresses on both research and ethical considerations. This seminar will highlight common mistakes made by applicants in Funding Research Applications and the "Application Form for Human Ethics Approval of Research Projects". I have gathered feedback from both Internal and External Reviewers to provide valuable insights. The discussion will encompass various topics, including: General Notes, and Questionnaire and Interview Guidelines on Funding Research Applications; Application Outline, Review Checklist, Methodology, Data Collection, Target Participants, Informed Consent, Identifiable Information, Undue Influence and Inducement, Attachments, and Declaration on the Ethics Application Form.

[h1] About Us

[h1] Data Science Research Centre for Social Policies and Services

[h3] About Us

[h5] The Data Science Research Centre at Saint Francis University was established in January 2022, with the support of aRGC Institutional Development Scheme (IDS) Research Infrastructure Grant.

[h5] The Research Centre will build a small team of data scientist and engineers, to work on inter-disciplinary and applied data science research problem, with a focus on the social policies and services area initially. We collaborate with faculty members and research staff at SFU as well as other institutions. We also seek to work with NGOs and other government and non-government organizations that are involved with social services and policies, have data and real-world problems. The goal is to not only publish academic papers, but also make real-world impact.

[h3] Mission

[h5] The mission of the Data Science Research Center (DSRC) is to help expand the research capability of SFU by cultivating and supporting research in this inter-disciplinary area. Initially, the focus will be in the social services and social policy area, as this is a well-established academic area for SFU, and SFU has good connections to the social services community. Our goal is to do applied, innovative and socially meaningful research by applying data science methodologies to the social science area.

# Saint Francis University - S.K. Yee Healthcare Research Centre

With the support of the RGC Institutional Development Scheme (IDS) Research Infrastructure Grant (UGC/IDS11/15), the Healthcare Research Centre (HRC) at the S.K. Yee School of Health Sciences, Saint Francis University was founded in January 2016. The HRC works closely to nurture and support academic staff of the School, who are at different career stages, through the ten research theme groups which composes of convenors and members. The HRC focuses on conducting applied research grounded in community and primary healthcare, gerontology, health and well-being, education, and translational research in pharmacology & pharmacy. Leveraging on the competency of scholars from nursing, pharmacy, and physiotherapy, it implements a community practice model: CommunityHealth@SFU and Caritas St. Francis Pharmacy through which the data of consenting clients who have received community healthcare services at SFU have been collected for analyses. The HRC also supports student research and research outputs. Our research projects also engage research partners from within our local and international collaborative links. Our research aspirations in the next five years are to: Establish a united research culture and supportive environment to support staff, Increase staff visibility in grants, publications & conferences, Become a research active School, Conduct research to contribute to society, teaching and learning, and Gain national and international recognition in our research endeavours.

[h1] Caregiving Research and Development Centre

[h2] About us

[h2] Objectives

The Caregiving Research and Development Centre (CRC) at Saint Francis University has been established in January 2025, with support from the Institutional Development Scheme (IDS) Research Infrastructure Grant of the Research Grants Council (RGC). The CRC adopts an interinstitutional and interdisciplinary approach to enhance academic research, consultancy, teaching and learning, service development and policy formulation in caregiving for frail elders and individuals with disabilities. The Centre focuses on the diverse needs of caregivers in different stages of caregiving journal, examine both positive and negative aspects of caregiving, promote strength-based and empowerment approach in caregiver support, ultimately providing evidence-based alternatives and ideas on government policy, social services, health care and community resources.

The CRC conducts research studies into caregiving policies and practices, facilitating knowledge exchange through regular conferences and workshops. Collaboration with local, mainland and international universities, practitioners, government bodies, and non-profit organizations will be essential in addressing caregiving challenges and shaping the research agenda. The Centre aims to translate research findings into practical solutions and innovative strategies that benefit caregivers, practitioners, and policymakers. Through these efforts, the CRC aspires to create a measurable impact that extends beyond academia, ultimately benefiting the broader caregiving community.

[h1] About Us

[h1] About Us

Saint Francis University (SFU) works closely side by side with Caritas Bianchi College of Careers (CBCC) striving to become the Saint Francis University. The two-college system provides diploma, higher diploma and degree programmes for students to acquire professional training and higher education qualifications. It fills the gap of the current one-track education, giving a hope of upward mobility to the younger generation.

Having been awarding degrees since 2011 for over a dozen of academic programmes, such as Nursing, Social Work, Bilingual Studies, Hotel Management, Accountancy, Corporate Management, and Digital Entertainment, SFU aspires to be a well-respected and internationally recognized institution.

SFU, formerly Caritas Institution of Higher Education / Caritas Francis Hsu College, and CBCC enjoy a long tradition as caring institutions, being established in 1985 and 1971 respectively. Our mission is to produce graduates who are not only academically and professionally well-educated but who can also contribute to the social and moral well-being of the community.

SFU’s holistic education encourages young people to look at issue from different points of view, impart positive life values and the can-do spirit for personal development, pursue excellence through unceasing self-improvement, and for winning at the finish line. Our motto is Ad Destinatum Prosequor (自強不息).

[h1] Welcome Message

[h1] Welcome Message

[h2] Message from the former Chairperson of the Board of Governors of Caritas Institute of Higher Education and Caritas Bianchi College of Careers

Dear Brothers and Sisters in Christ,

Youths have all kinds of dreams. However, the passion of many fades away with the test of time, obstacles and failures.

Young people are our hope, and much-needed pillars of our society. Yet, as part of the Church and as part of society, we have to ask, “How much have we invested in them?”

Caritas Institute of Higher Education (CIHE/the Institute) has been providing quality education for these future pillars and giving second chances to those who have stumbled. We look forward to the Institute becoming the Saint Francis University in the future. The Institute is dedicated to guiding young people to the road of success, through professional training, and providing them with a platform to discover their strengths and fulfill their potential. As the Catholic university in Hong Kong, the Institute aims to instill high professional moral and good values of the Church in the next generation, who can then contribute fully to society.

Since the launch of the Seventh Matching Grant Scheme offered by the HKSAR Government in August 2017, we have successfully secured the “floor” of HK$12 million in matching grant on a dollar-to-dollar matching basis (i.e. a $1 to $1 matching ratio). We sincerely thank all supporters for their contributions. However, we still have to work harder as donations beyond the floor will be matched on one-dollar-for-two-dollar basis (i.e. $1 government grant for every $2 of donation), up to the “ceiling” of HK$100 million while the available matching fund lasts.

Even with the matching grant, it remains a challenge for us to raise the remaining balance of the construction cost of HK$800 million for the new CIHE campus, and an additional HK$200 million for the university start-up operation. We hope that all of you who share our vision of building society and the church will contribute generously, and support us in prayers and actions to realise the Saint Francis University!

May Christ bring grace, reward and joy to you and your family! Thank you!

Most Rev Michael YeungLate Bishop of Hong KongFormer Chairperson, Board of GovernorsCaritas Institute of Higher Education

[h1] CIHE Post-Event Report on DELF 2023

[h1] CIHE Post-Event Report on DELF 2023

[h1] CIHE Post-Event Report on DELF 2023

As the Supporting Institute for Digital Entertainment Leadership Forum (DELF) 2023 (數碼娛樂領袖論壇), the Cyberport's flagship event on digital entertainment and esports, Caritas Institute of Higher Education (CIHE) is delighted to see the event was successfully held on 25 - 27 August 2023.  DELF 2023 attracted over 3,500 attendees, including government officials, corporates, startups, and the general public for the three-day programme.  It featured more than 40 digi-tainment venture across various domains, including gaming, sports and esports, music, arts and culture, education, and lifestyle, which provided a mind-blowing carnival-like experience for the participants.

The senior management of Hong Kong Cyberport Management Company Limited (the Cyberport) expressed their appreciation for CIHE's support in making DELF 2023 a success.  Teamed up with the School of Computing and Information Sciences (SCIS), the Ip Ying To Lee Yu Yee School of Humanities and Languages (SHL), the Fundraising Office and about 20 student ambassadors, CIHE showcased the Institute's strength on Artificial Intelligence (AI) development at the event.  It included SCIS's demos on Intelligent Sketch (快速智慧素描), Intelligent Painter (智慧構圖：協助你創製沙龍作品), Anime photo stylization, and SHL's presentation on Chinese-English Food and Drinks Translation System (漢英中國飲食詞匯翻譯系統).

CIHE was fortunate to be connected with the industry and business counterparts through DELF 2023.  The post-event meetings have been arranged with Ir Eric Chan Sze-yuen, Chief Public Mission Officer of the Cyberport, Mr Wren Chao of Art Great Creation Limited, Mr Thomas Jor of ATTA Technologies, and Mr Joe Chan of ICT-in-Physical Education Foundation Limited.  Connections with Mr Alan Cheung Yick-Lun of Grandion Group, and Mr Purehay Au-Yeung of Pure Studio have likewise been forged.

Highlights of follow-up meeting:Following on the successfully experience of DELF 2023, Ir Eric Chan Sze-yuen the Chief Public Mission Officer of the Cyberport together with his colleague Mr Ricky Choi paid a visit to CIHE campus on 18 September 2023.  The meeting with Ir Chan was very fruitful as promising collaborations and the youth development programme would possibly go further in new ventures between CIHE and the Cyberport.Prepared by the Fundraising OfficeCaritas Institute of Higher Education20 September 2023

The HKSAR Government launched a new round of theResearch Matching Grant Scheme (RMGS), committing a total ofHK$1.5 billionover a four-year period from1 May 2025 to 30 April 2029.

The RMGS is designed to enhance research capacity and development across the higher education sector.  Under the Scheme:

Donations received bySaint Francis University (SFU)for research-related purposes are eligible for matching grants, with no restrictions on academic disciplines.RMGScovers the eight UGC-funded universities and thirteen local self-financing degree-awarding institutions. Each institution may receive amaximum matching grant of HK$200 million, allocated on afirst-come, first-served basis.

We sincerely invite you tosupport SFUby donating toward this initiative. Your contribution will multiply our research resources and advance SFU's institutional development.

He is a beautiful race horse but ran very badly in all races. He retired early with 0 rating because he felt nervous racing with a big group of race horses. The owner did not give up hopes on him and sent him to a stable in Perth, Australia for training. Only after one year, he won the Overall Championship for the Year in Australia for his age in the Young Horse Dressage and Jumping Competition in Australia. He looked extremely smart in the Award Blanket. As he grew, he continued to win numerous awards in Dressage and Jumping competitions. Team Tonic could not perform when he competed in a group setting. However, he out-performed his competitors in a different setting when he did it his way. His story inspires that there is always talent within ourselves so do not despair on failure. Discover our talent and work on developing it for a bright future. Success is in our hands. Description | An impressive and exceptional underglaze-blue and famille-verte 'doucai' (contrasting colors) tea bowlThis fine tea bowl, rising from a short straight foot to flared angled sides and everted rim, painted to the interior in rich coral red, blue and white, gilt the active dragon striding in pursuit of a flaming pearl amidst cloud scrolls, dragon body further along the exterior side among the coral red cloud scrolls.According to historical records, 'doucai' (contrasting colors) began in the Ming Xuande, but very rare can find.The 'doucai' wares appeared in the years of Ming Xuande , and it was brilliant in ChengHua period, most of them were cup, plate, bowl, dish and small objects. Emperor ChengHua was keen on painting, porcelain deeply, because of his weakness character, he was not interested on any intense colour porcelain, but like the soft and elegant colour......'doucai' porcelain.The most famous porcelain during the ChengHua years was the 'chicken cup' and the love story between the Emperor ChengHua and his 'Noble Consort Wàn', 'Noble Consort Wàn' liked the 'doucai' chicken cup very deeply. As the 'doucai' wares was favorited by the royal family, ChengHua 'doucai' porcelain became the hottest collectible piece, it was not only become the main steam on imperial collection, and also became famous art treasures on the fine quality of 'doucai'.In Qing Dynasty, Emperors Kangxi, Yongzheng, Qianlong also has a lot of fine imperial collection comparable to the Ming's 'doucai', even some were larger wares. Most of the Qing dynasty 'doucai' porcelain were very fine work on the painting, but lost the elegance character from Ming's with. Also, lots of Ming's 'doucai' imitation found in Qing Dynasty production.[GuangXu to HongXian period]

# Saint Francis University - University titling: FAQ for Current Students

The Chief Executive in Council approved the university status of Caritas Institute of Higher Education (CIHE) on 9 January 2024. CIHE is now renamed "Saint Francis University" in English and “聖方濟各大學” in Chinese.

[h1] University titling: FAQ for Current Students

[h1] Registry

[h2] University titling: FAQ for Current Students

The arrangements will be announced in due course.

Transcripts under the name of Saint Francis University have been issued since June 2024.

Graduation certificates under the name of Saint Francis University have been issued since December 2024. If you receive a graduation certificate issued during the transition period, the University is pleased to offer a standard University Titling Statement for graduates holding CIHE certificates issued on or after 27 May 2011.To apply for this Statement, please submit your applicationhere. For any inquiries, please contact the Registry atregistry@sfu.edu.hk.

No, students will continue to receive government subsidy if the programme is subsidized by the government under SSSDP/NMTSS.

No, students who need financial assistance may submit applications to the Financial Assistance Scheme for Post-secondary Students (FASP) and the Non-means-tested Loan Scheme for Post-secondary Students (NLSPS).

No, eligible students will continue to receive scholarships.  Please refer to thewebsiteof Saint Francis Universityfor details.

Past Events Caritas Secondary Schools Visit to Saint Francis University On 11 February 2026, Saint Francis University (SFU) had the pleasure of hosting a campus tour and exchange session for the administrative staff from Caritas Secondary Schools across Hong Kong. During the visit, our guests have participated in a guided tour to learn more about SFU's teaching facilities, including the well‑equipped Physiotherapy Laboratory, Dispensing Laboratory, Design and Film & Media Production Studios, Hotel Simulation Rooms, and the Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. The group also attended an information session arranged by the Recruitment and Engagement Team, and learned more about SFU's unique positioning as an Applied Science University, its programme offerings, and the career prospects of its graduates. We believe the visit has provided the team from Caritas Secondary Schools a more comprehensive understanding of SFU's articulation pathway structure and scholarship schemes available to their DSE graduating students. Tak Sun Secondary School Teacher Group Visits Saint Francis University On 5 December 2025, a group of six teachers from Tak Sun Secondary School visited Saint Francis University (SFU) for the first time. As an all-boys secondary school, Tak Sun places a strong emphasis on science and computing, making this visit particularly relevant. The teachers attended an introductory talk that provided insights into our campus, academic offerings, and the distinctions between traditional universities and universities of applied sciences. They toured our state-of-the-art nursing and physiotherapy labs, where some of their graduates are enrolled for the academic year 2025-2026. Additionally, our Yam Pak Charitable Foundation School of Computing and Information Sciences (CIS) hosted an engaging talk moderated by Mr Paul Hodgson and Dr William Cheung. They shared courses in AI, DET, and Crime and Security, highlighting potential career paths in these fields. The visiting teachers found the experience highly informative and appreciated the opportunity to explore the possibilities SFU offers their students. Saint Francis University Participates in Lantau Island Joint-School HKDSE Mock Exam Released Day 2025 On 3 December 2025, Saint Francis University (SFU) participated in the Lantau Island Joint-School HKDSE Mock Exam Released Day 2025, an annual event organized by HKSKH Tung Chung Integrated Services. The event provides a valuable platform for over 500 students and teachers from 6 participating schools – Buddist Fat Ho Memorial School, HKFEW Wong Cho Bau Secondary School, Ho Yu College and Primary School (Sponsored by Sik Sik Yuen), Ling Liang Church E Wun Secondary School, PLK Mrs Ma Kam Ming Cheung Fook Sien College, Tung Chung Catholic School – to gain insights into higher education opportunities and the career prospects across various industries. It also helps students to prepare for post-HKDSE applications and interviews. We have invited Mr. Gary Lam from the Caritas Bianchi College of Careers Irene Lam Department of Design, and Mr. Stephen So from Yam Pak Charitable School of Computing and Information Science represented SFU and engaged with the HKDSE students. A key highlight of the event was the Design Talk delivered by Mr. Gary Lam, Senior Lecturer (Graphic Design) cum Head, Department of Design. The session provided an overview for students interested in design, offering a clearer understanding of available programmes and career pathways in graphic, fashion or interior architect. Participants were very attentive, enjoyed the entire session, and actively engaged with our speaker. Saint Francis University Participates in the Joint-School Higher Education Expo and Thematic Talk on Applied Science University On 29 November 2025, Saint Francis University (SFU) participated in the Joint-School Higher Education Expo 2025 organized by HKSKH Bishop Hall Secondary School. There were an estimate of 500 Form 5 and 6 students, teachers and parents participated in this event; they are from HKSKH Bishop Hall Secondary School, Po Kok Secondary School, St Stephen's Church College and China Holiness College. Multiple activities were taking place simultaneously during the event. As part of the event, a thematic talk on Applied Science University (UAS) was held for parents. On 11 February 2026, Saint Francis University (SFU) had the pleasure of hosting a campus tour and exchange session for the administrative staff from Caritas Secondary Schools across Hong Kong.

During the visit, our guests have participated in a guided tour to learn more about SFU's teaching facilities, including the well‑equipped Physiotherapy Laboratory, Dispensing Laboratory, Design and Film & Media Production Studios, Hotel Simulation Rooms, and the Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. The group also attended an information session arranged by the Recruitment and Engagement Team, and learned more about SFU's unique positioning as an Applied Science University, its programme offerings, and the career prospects of its graduates.

We believe the visit has provided the team from Caritas Secondary Schools a more comprehensive understanding of SFU's articulation pathway structure and scholarship schemes available to their DSE graduating students.

On 5 December 2025, a group of six teachers from Tak Sun Secondary School visited Saint Francis University (SFU) for the first time. As an all-boys secondary school, Tak Sun places a strong emphasis on science and computing, making this visit particularly relevant.

The teachers attended an introductory talk that provided insights into our campus, academic offerings, and the distinctions between traditional universities and universities of applied sciences. They toured our state-of-the-art nursing and physiotherapy labs, where some of their graduates are enrolled for the academic year 2025-2026.

Additionally, our Yam Pak Charitable Foundation School of Computing and Information Sciences (CIS) hosted an engaging talk moderated by Mr Paul Hodgson and Dr William Cheung. They shared courses in AI, DET, and Crime and Security, highlighting potential career paths in these fields.

The visiting teachers found the experience highly informative and appreciated the opportunity to explore the possibilities SFU offers their students.

On 3 December 2025, Saint Francis University (SFU) participated in the Lantau Island Joint-School HKDSE Mock Exam Released Day 2025, an annual event organized by HKSKH Tung Chung Integrated Services.

The event provides a valuable platform for over 500 students and teachers from 6 participating schools – Buddist Fat Ho Memorial School, HKFEW Wong Cho Bau Secondary School, Ho Yu College and Primary School (Sponsored by Sik Sik Yuen), Ling Liang Church E Wun Secondary School, PLK Mrs Ma Kam Ming Cheung Fook Sien College, Tung Chung Catholic School – to gain insights into higher education opportunities and the career prospects across various industries. It also helps students to prepare for post-HKDSE applications and interviews.

We have invited Mr. Gary Lam from the Caritas Bianchi College of Careers Irene Lam Department of Design, and Mr. Stephen So from Yam Pak Charitable School of Computing and Information Science represented SFU and engaged with the HKDSE students.

A key highlight of the event was the Design Talk delivered by Mr. Gary Lam, Senior Lecturer (Graphic Design) cum Head, Department of Design. The session provided an overview for students interested in design, offering a clearer understanding of available programmes and career pathways in graphic, fashion or interior architect. Participants were very attentive, enjoyed the entire session, and actively engaged with our speaker.

On 29 November 2025, Saint Francis University (SFU) participated in the Joint-School Higher Education Expo 2025 organized by HKSKH Bishop Hall Secondary School. There were an estimate of 500 Form 5 and 6 students, teachers and parents participated in this event; they are from HKSKH Bishop Hall Secondary School, Po Kok Secondary School, St Stephen's Church College and China Holiness College.

Multiple activities were taking place simultaneously during the event. As part of the event, a thematic talk on Applied Science University (UAS) was held for parents. Representatives from four institutions – SFU, Metropolitan University, Tung Wah College and THEi – sharing insights on UAS programme offerings and their QF / professional recognition. SFU was represented by Dr. Michael Lai, Assistant Professor at the Rita Tong School of Business and Hospitality Management.

There different interactive tasting programmes were also conducted on-site by SFU, allowing students to explore areas in business management, social care and virtual content development. Representatives from Rita Tong School of Business and Hospitality Management, Felizberta Lo Padilla Tong School of Social Science, and Yam Pak Charitable Foundation School of Computing and Information Science hosted these engaging activities.  These activities demonstrated our strong commitment to helping students make informed choices for their higher education and career pathway.

At the SFU information booth, the recruitment team provided support to answer participants' inquiries, such as programme offerings and application procedures. Students, teachers, and parents received information on relevant topics such as articulation pathways and fee-waived applications.

Saint Francis University ("SFU") participated in the 3rd Ming Pao Greater Bay Area (GBA) Hong Kong School Education Expo, held from November 28 to 30, 2025 at AsiaWorld‑Expo.

Over the 3 days, approximately 100 visitors approached the University's booth. Many expressed strong interest in SFU, particularly as the institution is relatively new to mainland Chinese audiences. Through face‑to‑face conversations, our representatives introduced the University's academic strengths, programme offerings, and student support philosophy, enabling visitors to gain a better understanding of the opportunities available at SFU.

Participation in the Expo further strengthened the University's visibility in the Greater Bay Area and laid the groundwork for future connections with students and families seeking diverse and high‑quality study options.

On 27 October 2025, Dr Kat Leung, Vice‑President (Administration) and Institute Secretary of Saint Francis University (SFU), and Dr Aries Chan, Assistant Director of the Public Affairs Office (Recruitment and Engagement) and Head of the Global and Mainland Engagement Division, visited San Wui Commercial Society Chan Pak Sha School (SWCS Chan Pak Sha School) for an exchange visit.

Principal Ms Chan Ying‑ying and her team warmly welcomed the SFU team, and accompanied them on a campus tour, and shared in‑depth insights into the school's educational philosophy and distinctive features.

During the campus visit, Principal Chan shared the school's focus on balanced, whole‑person development - cultivating student's intellectual growth, physical and mental well‑being. To achieve this goal, the school combines rigorous academic standards with a wide range of co‑curricular programmes to support student development: the Football, Basketball and Volleyball Teams; Wind Band; Martial Arts Team; and Drum Team.

The Drum Team won the Silver Award at the Joint School Music Contest 2025, and the Dragon‑boat Team earned the third place in the 2025 Hong Kong International Dragon Boat Invitation Race - Secondary School Championship and Chairman's Shield.

The school also organises annual off‑campus learning trips to mainland cities to explore technology industries and historical culture, visits to Hong Kong International Airport to learn about operations and industry development, tours to Ocean Park for ecological education, and community service activities such as grooming services for elderly and grassroots groups, all of which foster students' organisational skills, teamwork and community care.

In the exchange, Dr Leung shared detailed perspectives on SFU admission pathways, cultural exchange opportunities and student development support, and both sides engaged in a fruitful exchange of views. Principal Chan emphasised the school's strong commitment to students' further education planning and holistic quality development and expressed interest in establishing a long‑term collaboration with Saint Francis University. The visit laid the groundwork for future cooperation, with both institutions indicating a desire to build partnership initiatives to support student growth and contribute to educational development.

On November 2, 2025, Saint Francis University participated in the JUPAS Info Day organised by Ming Pao at the Kowloon Shangri-La Hotel in Hong Kong. Our academic staff and representatives from the Public Affairs Office (Recruitment & Engagement Team) engaged with approximately 250 visitors, primarily Form 5 and Form 6 students and their parents. Many expressed strong interest in our programmes and articulation pathways, as well as inquiries related to the application procedures.

One of the highlights of the day was a 15-minute programme talk conducted by Dr. Carol Chan, Associate Dean of the School of Health Sciences, which attracted around 40 attendees. Dr. Chan shared insights into our programmes related to Health Sciences and the future career development. The entire event provided a valuable opportunity for local students and their parents who are interested in applying, enhancing their awareness of the our offerings, articulation pathways and potential career pathways.

On October 28, 2025, we were thrilled to host a group of dedicated teachers from Cheng Chek Chee Secondary School at Saint Francis University. This visit provided a fantastic opportunity to share our mission and introduce our programmes and articulation pathways.

The discussions were not just informative but also inspiring, as we exchanged ideas with educators who share our passion for supporting students in their career planning and further studies. We truly value these connections and the collaborative spirit they bring!After the talk, the teachers also participated in our taster programme organized by the S.K. Yee School of Health Sciences, and they greatly enjoyed this experience.

Saint Francis University participated in the Greater Bay Area Education and Talent Expo 2025 organised by the Hong Kong Teenager All-Round Development Association at Hall 3FG of the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre from October 3 to 5, 2025, to strengthen the University's visibility across the Greater Bay Area.Representatives from each of our six academic faculties, along with administrative support staff, were present to engage with the visitors and answer their enquiries. Through face-to-face discussions and video presentations, they introduced the University's diverse programmes, advanced teaching facilities, and its holistic student support and learning philosophy. The Expo enabled attendees to gain a deeper understanding of our institutional strengths and equipped them to plan their future academic and career pathways.

Saint Francis University participated in the Ming Pao Education Expo 2025, held from July 12 to 13, 2025 and organised by Ming Pao Education. The event attracted approximately 12,000 visitors, including students, parents and education sectors. As one of Hong Kong's applied science universities, the university offers a broad range of academic pathways, from foundation diplomas to master's degree programmes.

Caritas Institute of Higher Education (CIHE) and Caritas Bianchi College of Careers (CBCC) Joint Graduation Ceremony had been held on January 2023. A total of 1,023 graduates from both institutes obtained their degrees and diplomas and commenced their new journeys.

Graduation is not an end but another start of a journey.  CIHE & CBCC share the joyfulness with our fellow graduates and wish them a brighter future.  It is hoped that our graduates would continue their success with our motto – Ad Destinatum Persequor in their hearts.  We also open our doors for the return of the alumni.

School principal and teachers from Newman Catholic College visited CIHE&CBCC campuses on their Teachers' Development Day on 26 March 2021. The Day started with an introductory speech by Dr. Kat LEUNG, Vice-President of CIHE, followed by campus tours and visit to teaching facilities such as laboratories of Physiotherapy, Nursing and Artificial Intelligence programmes. This allowed teachers to better understand the articulation pathways and programmes offered by CIHE&CBCC.

From 6 to 13 July, Rita Tong Liu School of Business and Hospitality Management and Career Centre had jointly organized 8 free webinars. A total of 8 renowned guest speakers were invited to share the view of the impacts of COVID-19 on the Hong Kong and Global economy and business survival, and gave advices to the participants who come from various industries as well as the fresh graduates.

To enhance engagement with CIHE&CBCC students, Student Affairs Office held a series of online live sessions via Zoom during March to May. Staff members were invited to share and interact with students on different topics. Sessions include:

On 7/7 2019 CIHE held its first ever CIHE "Pray-ground", a community event gathering students, parents and parishioners alike to show our support to the HKDSE students prior to their result release day.Approximately 450 people join this fun-filled Sunday afternoon, and our campus was transformed into a "pray-ground" completed with mini game booths, art workshops and a seminar on adolescent psychology. Accompanied by our honoured guests Catholic Artistes Ms Maggie Chan and Mr Chan Wing Chun, Fr. Dominic Chan led the opening ceremony, which included the lighting of the "Wall of Blessings" donated by our alumni Mr. and Mrs. Lee.  It was followed by personal sharings of our esteemed guests on handling life challenges. After which Auxiliary Bishop Joseph Ha came and celebrated special mass, dedicated to all HKDSE students and their families. The day ended with a concert organized by Christ Youth Action and Freeup Music.Many thanks to all our partners who dedicated their time and efforts, making this event a great success and all the best to all HKDSE students in their future academic pursuits!Event highlight:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tuz01vl6g_8&feature=youtu.be

The Information Day of CIHE and CBCC was successfully held on 9 and 10 November 2018. Over 600 visitors including students, teachers and parents participated in a wide range of activities organised by our Schools and Departments such as admission talks, consultation sessions, campus tours, themed seminars, workshops and demonstrations.

The delegation from the Federations of Parent-Teacher Associations of 18 Districts paid a visit to CIHE & CBCC on 6 Oct 2018, learning more about our programmes as well as our teaching and learning facilities. Spending a morning at our campus, they mingled and had luncheon with our academic staff members.

Thank you for their interest in and support for CIHE & CBCC!

On 6 June 2018, CIHE has received HK$5 million donations from Alfar Charitable Fund and GS Charity Foundation respectively in support of two professorships in the School of Business and Hospitality Management.

Alfar Charitable Trust also made a one-off donation of HK$1 million to set up a scholarship for students in need to complete their 4-year degree programmes.

Thank you for the support of Alfar Charitable Fund and GS Charity Foundation!

# Saint Francis University - Senior Management Positions

Duties Reporting to the President, the Vice-President (Academic and Quality Assurance) is a principal officer of the University, responsible for providing strategic leadership and institutional oversight in quality assurance, academic governance and standards, and external accreditation. The appointee will oversee the planning, development, implementation and evaluation of academic programmes to ensure academic quality, relevance and sustainable growth. Working closely with senior management, academic leaders and key stakeholders, the appointee will contribute to institutional planning, policy formulation and continuous quality enhancement, and represent the University in engagement with accreditation authorities, professional bodies and partner institutions. The role also entails fostering a robust culture of quality, evidence-based review and ongoing enhancement in support of the University's mission and long-term development. Appointment Criteria The ideal candidate should possess: A bachelor's degree, preferably a postgraduate qualification. Substantial relevant senior leadership experience in local and/ or overseas higher education institutions. Proven track record of strong leadership in accreditation, regulatory compliance, and academic governance, with sound knowledge of the Hong Kong and regional higher education regulatory environment, particularly in self-financing or non-UGC-funded institutions. Excellent communication, negotiation, project development and implementation skills, as well as outstanding people and team-building skills. High integrity and a commitment to innovate and implement best practices. Excellent command of written and spoken English; proficiency in Chinese, including Putonghua, is an advantage. [h2] Part 2: Credit Transfer Arrangement for Receiving Programme

In general, applicants who either possess sub-degree qualifications or have completed one year of study in degree programmes at local or overseas universities recognized by CIHE may be considered grantingAdvanced Standing. Advanced Standing gives applicant credit for his/her prior study and is granted in consideration of the relevance of the student's general learning experience. It enables a study period to be partially shortened.

Applicants do not need to apply forAdvanced Standing, and the process is initiated by the Institute/College. The exact number of Advanced Standing credits to be granted depends on the level, the performance and the degree of contents matching of the prior study and is subject to the final decision of the Academic Head with justification(s) and the endorsement by Registry at admission.

Students may also apply forCourse Exemptionfrom taking any individual course if they have obtained qualifications/learnings which are recognised by the Institute as equivalent to those offered by the Institute.

ForCourse Exemption, it will be granted on a course-by-course basis. Applications must be made in the prescribed form "Application for Course Exemption" together with supporting documents such as course outline and syllabus.

Overall speaking,not more than 50%of the credit requirement for the academic award may be transferred from any approved tertiary institute and CIHE reserves the right not to grant Advanced Standing / Course Exemption for courses which do not correspond to the courses offered by a CIHE degree programme. For the approved Advanced Standing / Course Exemption, no grade will be given but credits will be granted for fulfilling the number of credits for graduation. Students should also note that such credits will NOT be included in the calculation of Grade Point Average.

Gale Academic OneFile connects learners to the information they’re looking for with tools that make discovery fast and easy. This premier periodical resource provides millions of articles from scholarly journals and other authoritative sources with extensive coverage in key subject areas, such as biology, chemistry, criminal justice, economics, environmental science, history, marketing, political science, and psychology.

Academic Search Ultimate is a multi-disciplinary research database that provides more than 12,000 full-text periodicals, among which 10,600 are peer-reviewed journals. In addition to academic journals and magazines, it also includes current videos from Associated Press, books, reports, conference papers and government documents that can meet the needs of scholars in nearly every academic discipline.

Academic Video Online is a comprehensive and multidisciplinary platform with more than 85,000 streaming videos, covering topics in education, business and economics, film, music, nursing, psychology, and more.

AccessPharmacy provides pharmacy students with access to drug information, cases, videos, and leading pharmacy textbooks that will establish an important foundation for learning.

AccessPhysiotherapy is a comprehensive online physiotherapy resource that integrates over 50 leading physical therapy textbooks, more than 2,200 NPTE related self-assessment questions, procedure and exercise videos, images and a unique cadaver dissection tool.

The ACM Digital Library is a comprehensive database focused on the field of computing and information science. It features over 11,000 full-text collections of journals, conference proceedings, technical magazines & newsletter articles, covering a wide spectrum of topics such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine learning, Information Systems, Applications, Mathematics & Theories of Computing, Security & Privacy, Education, etc.

Active Reading is an interactive learning tool for developing reading skills, including prediction, vocabulary strategies, inference, skimming, topic sentences and more. It comes in six levels from elementary to advanced, with 10 units in each level. Each unit consists of a video introduction, controlled practice, comprehension exercises and concludes with a freer activity which expands on the topic.

Gale OneFile: Agriculture provides access to journals covering agriculture and its related fields. Researchers can access current and authoritative periodical content that spans the industry—from practical aspects of farming to cutting-edge scientific research in horticulture.

Anatomy TV.Anatomy & Physiologyis an interactive educational resource on human anatomy. It provides 20 comprehensive modules with 3D models, images, dissection slides, clinical case studies, video clips, information on the impact of aging and quizzes, covering various clinical areas and body systems.

PsycARTICLES is a psychology research database that provides full-text articles from journals published by the American Psychological Association, the APA Educational Publishing Foundation, the Canadian Psychological Association, and Hogrefe & Huber.

APA PsycBooks provides more than 4,600 full-text e-books covering the most current scholarly and professional titles published by American Psychological Association (APA) relating to psychology, child development, social behaviour, and more.

PsycInfo is a citation database published by the American Psychological Associations. It provides comprehensive indexing and abstracts of the international psychological literature from the 1800s to the present. Coverage includes all areas of psychology: applied psychology, communication, developmental psychology, educational psychology, experimental psychology, personality, psychological and physical disorders.

APA PsycTests is a database which provides access to more than 79,000 records of psychological tests and measures used in social and behavioural science research. It also includes supplementary information such as datasets, answer keys, scoring sheets and test manuals.

APA's PsycTHERAPY is a collection of over 900 streaming demonstration videos in psychotherapy. It features expert psychotherapists demonstrating various treatment approaches and provides methods showcasing common obstacles faced during therapy sessions.

Asia Art Archive is a repository of research materials in Asia Art. It includes primary source documents such as artists' writings and sketches, photographic documentation, video recordings and more.

 | ACM Digital LibraryThe ACM Digital Library is a comprehensive database focused on the field of computing and information science. It features over 11,000 full-text collections of journals, conference proceedings, technical magazines & newsletter articles, covering a wide spectrum of topics such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine learning, Information Systems, Applications, Mathematics & Theories of Computing, Security & Privacy, Education, etc.

 | Active Reading (Clarity English)Active Reading is an interactive learning tool for developing reading skills, including prediction, vocabulary strategies, inference, skimming, topic sentences and more. It comes in six levels from elementary to advanced, with 10 units in each level. Each unit consists of a video introduction, controlled practice, comprehension exercises and concludes with a freer activity which expands on the topic.

 | Agriculture (Gale OneFile)Gale OneFile: Agriculture provides access to journals covering agriculture and its related fields. Researchers can access current and authoritative periodical content that spans the industry—from practical aspects of farming to cutting-edge scientific research in horticulture.

 | Anatomy TV. Anatomy & PhysiologyAnatomy TV.Anatomy & Physiologyis an interactive educational resource on human anatomy. It provides 20 comprehensive modules with 3D models, images, dissection slides, clinical case studies, video clips, information on the impact of aging and quizzes, covering various clinical areas and body systems.

 | APA PsycARTICLES (ProQuest)PsycARTICLES is a psychology research database that provides full-text articles from journals published by the American Psychological Association, the APA Educational Publishing Foundation, the Canadian Psychological Association, and Hogrefe & Huber.

 | APA PsycBooks (ProQuest)APA PsycBooks provides more than 4,600 full-text e-books covering the most current scholarly and professional titles published by American Psychological Association (APA) relating to psychology, child development, social behaviour, and more.

 | APA PsycINFO (ProQuest)PsycInfo is a citation database published by the American Psychological Associations. It provides comprehensive indexing and abstracts of the international psychological literature from the 1800s to the present. Coverage includes all areas of psychology: applied psychology, communication, developmental psychology, educational psychology, experimental psychology, personality, psychological and physical disorders.

 | APA PsycTests (ProQuest)APA PsycTests is a database which provides access to more than 79,000 records of psychological tests and measures used in social and behavioural science research. It also includes supplementary information such as datasets, answer keys, scoring sheets and test manuals.

 | APA PsycTherapy (ProQuest)APA's PsycTHERAPY is a collection of over 900 streaming demonstration videos in psychotherapy. It features expert psychotherapists demonstrating various treatment approaches and provides methods showcasing common obstacles faced during therapy sessions.

 | Asia Art ArchiveAsia Art Archive is a repository of research materials in Asia Art. It includes primary source documents such as artists' writings and sketches, photographic documentation, video recordings and more.

[h1] Donor Stories - Passing on Love Through Education  2025-08-19

[h1] Donor Stories

[h2] Passing on Love Through Education

Donor: Mrs PoonAs a university founded on Catholic values, Saint Francis University (SFU) carries a unique mission among Hong Kong's esteemed universities — to provide access to higher education for underprivileged communities.  Through professional training, it empowers students to pursue their aspirations, establish a foothold in society, and build a brighter future, passing on love and hope to the next generations.

Looking back on my own educational journey, one personal experience remains deeply etched in my heart.  My parents separated when I was eight, and our family faced financial hardship.  Thankfully, the school showed compassion and allowed me to complete my secondary education with a symbolic tuition fee of just one dollar per month. Although I felt underprivileged due to our economic situation, I was profoundly moved by the silent support and care of my teachers.  A respected Chinese teacher once gifted me a sixteen-character motto: "No worry, no fear; no hesitation, no resentment; strive forward, aim high".  These words not only reflected a deep understanding of my circumstances but also became a spiritual anchor that helped me overcome adversity.

Thanks to the education I received at The University of Hong Kong, I resolved to give back to society through what I had learned — particularly by focusing on family relationship counselling.  I hope to support families in need through both theory and practice, especially in building strong marital relationships, including pre-marital counselling, nurturing post-marital bonds, and offering professional guidance to couples facing difficulties.  As a Catholic, I firmly believe that"responding to love with love"is not only the core of our faith but also a social responsibility that must be sustainably upheld.

Having been connected with SFU for over a decade, I deeply admire the founders' unwavering commitment to their original vision — to establish a university rooted in Catholic values despite many challenges.  I have witnessed the institution's continuous growth, its efforts to launch diverse programmes aligned with future development, and its dedication to nurturing talent for society.

I sincerely hope that kind-hearted individuals from all walks of life will join hands in supporting the promising development of SFU.

[h1] News - Saint Francis University Invited to Educational Exchange in Shanghai	Offering “Study in Hong Kong” Opportunities  2026-03-30

[h1] News

[h2] Saint Francis University Invited to Educational Exchange in Shanghai	Offering “Study in Hong Kong” Opportunities

From 28 to 30 March 2026, Saint Francis University ( "SFU"), represented by the Global and Mainland Engagement Division, was invited by the United Front Work Department of the Shanghai Municipal Committee to visit Shanghai for exchange and outreach activities. During the visit, the SFU delegation engaged in dialogue with local universities, and jointly explored future directions for Shanghai–Hong Kong educational cooperation.

On March 29, the SFU representatives visited Shanghai Ivy School and delivered an Information Session on Further Studies, which was attended by more than 30 students and parents. The Information Session provided a comprehensive introduction to SFU's programme offerings, admission requirements, and campus life. Dr Aries Chan, Head of the Global and Mainland Engagement Division, also offer oneonone advice based on students' interests and academic backgrounds, helping students and parents clearly plan their routes for further study in Hong Kong.

Ms. Wu Jie, Principal of Shanghai Ivy School, commended the Information Session enabled students and parents to gain a better understanding of Hong Kong's higher education system. The professional guidance provided by SFU addressed the core planning concerns of students aspiring to study in Hong Kong, and effectively conveyed SFU's ongoing commitment to promoting the "Study in Hong Kong" policy to both students and parents.

The visit reinforced Shanghai students' and parents' understanding of SFU, and strengthened institutional links between Shanghai and Hong Kong. Looking ahead, SFU will continue visiting cities across Mainland China to promote diverse pathways and opportunities for outstanding students to pursue studies in Hong Kong, and to further strengthen Shanghai–Hong Kong educational exchanges.

[h1] News - Saint Francis University Joining the National Education Study Tour for Hong Kong Higher Education Institutions, The Delegation Visited Wuhan for an Exchange 2026-03-25

[h1] News

[h2] Saint Francis University Joining the National Education Study Tour for Hong Kong Higher Education Institutions, The Delegation Visited Wuhan for an Exchange

Under the guidance of the Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Affairs Office of the Ministry of Education, the Department of Education and Technology of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the HKSAR, and the Hubei Provincial Department of Education, the Chinese University of Hong Kong organized a National Education Study Tour ("Study Tour") from 22 to 25 March 2026. The Study Tour aimed to deepen exchange and cooperation between Hong Kong and the Mainland in the field of higher education, and to strengthen collaboration in knowledge exchange, resources sharing and other academic initiatives.

The Study Tour brought together administrative personnel from Hong Kong higher education institutions (the "Delegation"). Dr. Fung Mo Chi, Associate Dean (Planning and Development) of the S.K. [h2] Saint Francis University participates in APAIE 2026  Further deepen international collaboration and promote the ‘Study in Hong Kong’ Brand

From 23 to 27 February, the 2026 Asia-Pacific Association for International Education (APAIE) Conference and Exhibition was successfully held at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. As an Applied Science University in Hong Kong, Saint Francis University (SFU) actively participated in this major international education event to connect with global academic network and advance the university's internationalisation strategy.

As one of the three major international education conferences in the world, this year's APAIE brought together nearly 3,000 international education leaders, experts, and scholars from over 70 countries. More than 450 universities and institutions joined the exhibition, with nearly 130 sessions of conferences and seminars exploring the latest trends in higher education. The event plays a crucial role in promoting the "Study in Hong Kong" Brand, expanding collaboration networks among Hong Kong's higher education institutions, and reinforcing Hong Kong's position as a premier global hub for higher education. Leveraging the APAIE platform, the SFU delegation introduced the University's educational philosophy and the distinctive strengths as an Applied Science University, showcased the excellence of Hong Kong's higher education and professional education sector, and promoted the "Study in Hong Kong" Brand worldwide.

During the event, SFU signed Memorandums of Understanding with Fu Jen Catholic University, Providence University, and BINUS University respectively, laying a solid foundation for future cooperation in areas such as faculty and student exchanges, academic collaboration, and joint research. The university also achieved fruitful outcomes and established collaborative intentions with various overseas institutions.

Looking ahead, SFU will continue to broaden platforms for international collaboration, expand its global partnership network, and elevate its international reputation, and foster high-calibre talents equipped with applied knowledge, professional competence, and global vision.

[h1] News - Saint Francis University Collaborates with GuangzhouHong Kong Teachers and Students to Advance Cultural and Technological Exchanges 2026-02-2

[h1] News

[h2] Saint Francis University Collaborates with GuangzhouHong Kong Teachers and Students to Advance Cultural and Technological Exchanges

To promote youth cultural exchange and technological collaboration in the Greater Bay Area and support youth development initiatives, the "錦繡越秀·藝航同行" Guangzhou-Hong Kong Youth Cultural and Technological Exchange Event—guided by the United Front Work Department of the CPC Yuexiu District Committee, hosted by Saint Francis University (SFU) and the Art Sailing Cultural Associations, co-organized by the Hong Kong Yuexiu Youth Federation, and sponsored by the Home and Youth Affairs Bureau of the HKSAR Government—was launched at SFU on February 2, 2026. A delegation of 40 teachers and students from Guangzhou Pui Ching Middle School will undertake a 4-day, 3-night cultural and technological exchange in Hong Kong, including visits to SFU, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Information Centre, the Hong Kong Museum of Art, and Phoenix TV.

The opening ceremony was honoured by the presence of distinguished guests, including Mr. Tang Fei, MH, Legislative Council Member (Functional Constituency – Education); Mr Xiong Xiaohua, Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the United Front Work Department of the CPC Yuexiu District Committee; Mr. Ho Chung Yip, Chairman of the Art Sailing Cultural Association; Ms. Wong Tsang, Vice Principal of Guangzhou Pui Ching Middle School; Dr. Leung Shi Ming, Vice-President (Administration) and Institute Secretary of SFU; Professor Chan Hing Hung Anthony, Dean of the School of Computing and Information Sciences; Dr. Chan Mei Sum, Assistant Director of the Public Affairs Office (Recruitment and Engagement) and Global and Mainland Engagement Division.

In her welcome speech, Dr. Leung Shi Ming emphasised that the event represents a key opportunity to expand technological and educational cooperation between Guangzhou and Hong Kong. Using culture and technology as bridges, it builds a solid platform for youth from both regions to learn from each other and foster mutual growth. Afterward, Mr. Ho Chung Yip, Mr. Xiong Xiaohua, and Mr. Tang Fei, MH shared their insights on youth development, technological innovation, cultural heritage, and regional collaboration, inspiring participants with practical guidance.

Following this, a sharing session was led by Professor Chan Hing Hung Anthony alongside Dr. Zhao Yingchao and Dr. Liu Xueting Tina from the School of Computing and Information Sciences. Under the topic"Impacts and Educational Directions in the Era of Artificial Intelligence", they illustrated key ideas through vivid examples and cutting-edge content, guiding participants to explore the development trends of artificial intelligence and everyday technologies. The delegation also visited the SFU campus to gain a deeper understanding about the university's facilities and learning environment. This exchange programme combined cultural visits with technological exploration, aiming to enhance participants' understanding of developments in both regions and to inspire innovative thinking among youth in the fields of culture and technology.

Looking ahead, Saint Francis University remain committed to hosting and engaging in diverse academic, cultural, and technology exchange programmes, leveraging its role as a knowledge hub to provide more inspiring learning experiences for teachers and students from mainland China and Hong Kong.

The University looks forward to building on this foundation to launch more impactful projects and to write a new chapter in shared educational growth.

[h1] News

[h2] Saint Francis University Visits Guangzhou to Deepen Greater Bay Area Educational Cooperation

On December 1, a delegation led by Professor Stephen Y.L. Cheung, President of Saint Francis University, together with Professor Chan Hing Hung Anthony, Dean of the Yam Pak Charitable Foundation School of Computing and Information Sciences, Dr. Wong Tik Tsuen Anthony (Associate Dean), Dr. Zhao Yingchao, Dr. Liu Xueting Tina, as well as representatives from the Public Affairs Office (Recruitment and Engagement Team) and the Global and Mainland Engagement Division - Dr. Aries Chan, Ms. Josephine Chan, and Ms. Wendy Siu - a total of 8 members, visited Guangzhou at the invitation of the United Front Work Department of the CPC Yuexiu District Committee.

This visit focused on key topics such as the establishment of a Mainland office, the alignment of educational resources, and the integration of cultural exchange. The delegation held in-depth discussions with the Yuexiu District United Front Work Department and the Education Bureau of Guangzhou Municipality, receiving positive responses and consensus on development, laying a solid foundation for the University to deepen its presence in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area and to serve national strategies.

During the visit, the delegation engaged in exchanges with the Yuexiu District United Front Work Department. Mr. Xiao Fengchun, Member of the Yuexiu District Party Committee and Director of the United Front Work Department, and Mr. Deng Weisheng, Deputy Inspector, personally received the delegation and warmly invited Saint Francis University to establish a Mainland office in Yuexiu District, expressing willingness to provide support and assistance for the University's development in the Mainland.

In the meeting, President Cheung emphasised the University's commitment to strengthening academic, research, and cultural exchanges with Mainland institutions, government agencies, and industry partners, exploring complementary resources and cooperative pathways. Both sides exchanged views on building cooperation platforms and directions, reached consensus on development, and agreed to steadily advance cooperation with the support of the Yuexiu District United Front Work Department. The office is expected to become an important bridge for the University to expand into the Mainland, enhance brand influence, and connect teaching, research, and industry resources.

This interaction is a concrete practice of implementing the "Outline Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area" and "Development Plan for Driving Higher Education Collaboration in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area", meeting the requirements of "building a collaborative higher education system" and "strengthening industry–education integration," and injecting quality educational resources and innovative strength into the construction of the Greater Bay Area.
